name: Alex Carr
life: “I learned my spouse's language badly enough to make their father laugh.” People around the bank steps know Alex by a small Monday habit. Alex takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
voice: I grew up elsewhere and married into this house. There's finally room to write my name at my adult height.
appearance: Alex has fine brows over wide-set eyes. Look for a high puff tied with plain cord. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a rust-colored canvas coat with a copper-colored clasp that has been repaired by hand. In conversation Alex leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations.
personality: Alex carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
agenda: To add the married-in family member's first pencil mark.
family: Anton March is Alex’s cousin raised in the same household. Alex asks before bringing somebody along. Anton can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *A ship without postcards*, Anton says, “I want a picture of the crane shadows. My kid thinks the ships do all the lifting.”
connections: Kai Shah. A newly married name and an old nickname fit on the same tracing.

reactions.response: Alex offers to help trace the height marks before work continues.
